title: Accounting Workflow Capacity Score
subtitle: Where are your hours actually leaking? An 18-question diagnostic for boutique accounting firms.

persona_selector.text: Which one are you in this firm?

answers.label: Owner or Managing Partner
Operations Lead or Practice Manager
Senior Accountant, Tax Lead, or IC

questions.text: When a new client signs the engagement letter, how does their information get into your practice management system?

answers.label: Manual re-typing from email or PDF
Form submission, but someone manually copies fields into one other system
Form submission, but someone copies fields into 2+ systems
Partial automation, one or two systems still need manual touch
One intake form populates everything (PM tool, CRM, document vault, billing)

questions.text: How many days between engagement signature and the client's onboarding pack landing in their inbox?

answers.label: 5+ days, often forgotten
4-5 days, depends entirely on workload
2-4 days, depends on who's covering
1-2 days, mostly consistent
Same day, automated

questions.text: Who chases missing documents (W-9s, prior returns, bank access, signed authorizations)?

answers.label: A senior accountant, in between billable work
A senior accountant, but only after a deadline slips
An admin, manually, via email
An admin using templated reminders in the PM tool
Automated reminders with a client portal

questions.text: When a client provides a list of bank accounts, vendors, or entities, how does it get structured for the team?

answers.label: Lives in an email thread
Pasted into a Word doc someone has to hunt for
Manually entered into a spreadsheet
Entered into a shared template, but not connected to workpapers
Structured at intake, flows into workpapers automatically

low.headline: Your intake is the bottleneck before work even starts
low.text: You're paying skilled accountants to do data entry. Every new client costs you 4-8 hours of senior time before a single billable task begins. This compounds across the book.
steps: Build a single intake form (Typeform, Tally, or Jotform) that writes directly to your PM tool via webhook or Zapier
Set up automated document request sequences with deadlines and reminders (no human in the loop until day 7)
Standardize the client information sheet so it becomes the source of truth for workpapers, billing, and CRM

mid.headline: Intake works, but it leaks at the handoffs
mid.text: You've solved the front door. The leak is between systems. Each manual re-entry is a place where data drifts and someone has to reconcile it later.
steps: Map every system that receives client data at onboarding and identify which two require duplicate entry
Connect those two systems via API or middleware (n8n, Make, Zapier) so intake writes once
Add a 48-hour automated check that flags any client missing required onboarding artifacts

high.headline: Intake is no longer a capacity question
high.text: You've removed onboarding as a constraint on growth. The next move is using intake data to pre-classify work and route engagements without partner triage.
steps: Use intake data to auto-assign engagement type, complexity tier, and lead accountant
Feed onboarding data into a capacity forecasting view so partners see workload 30 days out
Audit annually for new fields that could be captured upfront instead of mid-engagement

questions.text: What percentage of source documents (bank statements, receipts, payroll reports) arrive in a structured, parseable format?

answers.label: Under 25% - mostly PDFs, screenshots, photos of receipts
25-50% - some direct feeds, mostly unstructured
50-70% - mixed
70-80% - mostly structured with some exceptions
Over 80% - direct feeds, OCR'd, categorized at ingestion

questions.text: How does your team handle a client who drops a Dropbox link with 200 unsorted PDFs?

answers.label: A junior staffer spends a day sorting and renaming
A junior staffer sorts but only the most urgent items
We push back on the client, sometimes successfully
We have a naming convention the client mostly follows
Automated classification routes documents to the right workpaper folder

questions.text: When a bank feed breaks or a transaction misclassifies, who notices?

answers.label: The client, three weeks later, in a panic email
The accountant during month-end close, after work has piled up
The accountant during weekly review
An automated daily check flags it within 24 hours
Real-time monitoring with auto-classification rules that learn from corrections

questions.text: How long does it take a new staff member to find a specific document from a closed engagement two years ago?

answers.label: 30+ minutes, often impossible
15-30 minutes, requires asking someone senior
5-15 minutes with the right folder knowledge
Under 5 minutes via consistent folder structure
Searchable in seconds across all client engagements

low.headline: Your team is doing librarian work, not accounting work
low.text: Document chaos consumes 10-15 hours per accountant per week. The most expensive part is not the time. It is the senior judgment applied to filing instead of advisory work.
steps: Implement a document classification layer (Dext, Hubdoc, or a Claude-powered intake bot) that auto-routes incoming files
Standardize folder structure across all clients with a strict naming convention enforced at intake
Add weekly automated checks for missing or stale bank feeds so issues surface in days, not weeks

mid.headline: Document handling works but doesn't scale
mid.text: You have systems but they depend on individual discipline. The next person you hire will break them within 60 days unless the rules are enforced by software, not training.
steps: Move folder structure enforcement from human checklist to automated template provisioning on new engagements
Add OCR and classification on top of your existing document storage so search works across PDFs
Build a weekly anomaly report that flags missing documents before month-end close starts

high.headline: Documents are a data layer, not a chore
high.text: You've turned source documents into structured data. The use now is using that data for advisory insight, not just compliance.
steps: Use parsed document data to populate first-draft workpapers automatically
Surface anomalies and trends to clients proactively as part of monthly reporting
Audit your document pipeline quarterly for new document types that should be captured automatically

questions.text: How is your monthly close checklist tracked across the team?

answers.label: In someone's head or a private spreadsheet
A shared spreadsheet that nobody updates in real time
A shared checklist in the PM tool, updated manually
PM tool with status updates and assignments per client
Automated checklist with dependencies, deadlines, and roll-forward from prior periods

questions.text: When the same reconciliation question comes up across 30 clients, how is the answer captured?

answers.label: Re-derived from scratch each time
Asked to a senior, who answers from memory
Documented in a shared doc nobody reads
In a searchable knowledge base the team uses
In a knowledge base plus an AI assistant trained on firm precedent

questions.text: How are workpapers reviewed before sign-off?

answers.label: Partner reviews everything line by line
Partner reviews most files, samples the rest
Senior reviews, partner samples exceptions
Senior reviews using a standardized review checklist
Automated pre-checks flag exceptions, humans review only flagged items

questions.text: What happens when a client misses a deadline that blocks your close?

answers.label: We absorb the delay and work weekends
We escalate manually, often too late
Automated reminder, then manual escalation
Tiered reminders, partner notified at day 5
Automated escalation with re-pricing or scope-change trigger

low.headline: Your close process is held together by one or two people
low.text: The firm cannot grow past those people. When they take vacation, deadlines slip. When they leave, the firm has a crisis. Document the close before you hire the next accountant.
steps: Move the close checklist out of spreadsheets into your PM tool with explicit owners and due dates per task
Document the top 20 reconciliation patterns into a searchable internal wiki this quarter
Implement a tiered client deadline system with automated escalation, not partner-driven chase work

mid.headline: Your close runs, but partner review is the bottleneck
mid.text: You've systematized the work but not the review. Partners are spending billable hours on quality control that software can flag. This caps how many clients each partner can carry.
steps: Build automated pre-review checks that flag common workpaper exceptions before partner review
Codify the firm's top reconciliation precedents into a queryable knowledge base (Notion, Confluence, or AI-built)
Add a deadline-management layer that automatically re-prices or re-scopes when clients block your close

high.headline: Your close is a system, not a sprint
high.text: You've turned monthly close from an event into a process. use now means using the structured close data to power advisory conversations.
steps: Extract close-time data to identify which clients consistently consume the most senior time
Build client-specific dashboards from close data to drive monthly advisory conversations
Use AI to draft first-pass workpaper narratives, freeing seniors for judgment calls

questions.text: How does a client get an answer to a quick tax question?

answers.label: Email to partner, response in 3-7 days
Email to partner, response in 1-3 days
Email or PM tool, routed by admin, 24-hour SLA
Client portal with assigned owner and tracked SLA
Tiered intake with same-day resolution for routine questions

questions.text: How are monthly reports delivered to clients?

answers.label: PDF attached to an email, drafted manually each month
PDF from accounting software, lightly customized
Templated PDF report with consistent structure
Client portal with interactive reports and commentary
Auto-generated reports with AI-drafted commentary, partner reviewed

questions.text: When a client asks why a number changed month over month, how fast can you answer?

answers.label: Requires hours of digging by a senior
Within a few hours if the senior is available
Same day, by checking workpaper notes
Within an hour using structured commentary
Instantly via dashboard with drill-down

questions.text: How do you handle the post-tax-season check-in conversation with clients?

answers.label: We don't, we move on to the next deadline
Partners do it for the top 5 clients only
Manual outreach for tier-1 and tier-2 clients
Templated outreach with automated scheduling
Structured advisory program with automated touchpoints

low.headline: Clients judge you on responsiveness, not technical depth
low.text: Slow communication is the number one reason mid-market clients leave boutique firms. You are losing renewals to firms that answer faster, even when your work is better.
steps: Implement a client portal or PM-tool intake with a published SLA (24 hours for routine, same day for urgent)
Build a templated monthly report that pulls data from your accounting software so commentary is the only manual piece
Set up post-deadline outreach as an automated sequence, not a partner to-do

mid.headline: Communication is consistent but not differentiated
mid.text: You're delivering on the basics. The growth opportunity is moving from reactive answers to proactive insight, which is what justifies advisory pricing.
steps: Add monthly commentary to client reports that explains variance and surfaces one recommendation
Build a tiered SLA model where premium clients get faster response and proactive outreach
Move post-deadline check-ins from email to scheduled video conversations with a structured agenda

high.headline: Communication is now a moat
high.text: Your client experience is better than firms three times your size. The strategic move is productizing that experience so it scales without diluting quality.
steps: Package your advisory cadence into a named program with clear deliverables and a premium price
Use client interaction data to identify which clients are ready for an upsell or at risk of churn
Train an AI assistant on your firm's communication style so juniors draft client emails that sound like partners

questions.text: Do you know which clients are profitable and which are losing you money?

answers.label: No, we look at revenue per client, not margin
We have a rough sense based on partner gut feel
We track time per client but don't link it to fees
We have a profitability report we review quarterly
Live per-client profitability with automatic alerts on margin drops

questions.text: How is pricing set for new engagements?

answers.label: Whatever the client offered, or matched to a similar client
Hourly estimate multiplied by a target rate
Tiered pricing based on engagement complexity
Value-based pricing for advisory, scoped pricing for compliance
Dynamic pricing model informed by historical data on similar engagements

questions.text: When work backs up, what's the first lever you pull?

answers.label: Partner works the weekend
We hire a contractor under pressure
We push deadlines with clients
We rebalance work across the team using PM-tool data
Capacity forecasting flagged the issue weeks ago and we already adjusted

questions.text: What percentage of senior accountant time is spent on work a junior could do with the right system?

answers.label: More than 40%
Under 15%
Under 5%, seniors do senior work

low.headline: You're running blind on the metrics that determine whether the firm grows or stalls
low.text: Firms at your tier almost always discover that 20% of clients consume 60% of capacity at a loss. Without per-client profitability, every hiring decision is a guess.
steps: Implement time tracking at the client level for 90 days, even if you don't bill hourly, just to see where time actually goes
Calculate gross margin per client and identify the bottom quartile, then re-price or re-scope those engagements
Build a simple capacity forecasting view that shows committed work versus available hours 30 days out

mid.headline: You see the numbers but the firm doesn't act on them fast enough
mid.text: You have the data. The gap is the decision loop. Reviewing profitability quarterly means a bad engagement runs for 90 days before anyone notices.
steps: Set up automated alerts when a client's realized rate drops below threshold, partner notified within the week
Move from quarterly profitability review to a monthly partner conversation with a standing agenda
Move to value-based or scoped pricing for advisory work, decoupling fees from hours

high.headline: Capacity is a strategic asset, not a constraint
high.text: You're operating like a top-decile firm. The next move is using capacity data to expand into higher-margin advisory work and acquire the right clients, not just more clients.
steps: Use historical engagement data to build a pricing model that quotes new clients accurately and profitably
Identify the top 10% of your clients by profitability and design a referral program targeting their peers
Reinvest freed capacity into building productized advisory services with predictable margins

cta.headline: Want a partner who turns this score into an actual capacity plan?
cta.description: Most firms don't fail at the assessment. They fail at sequencing. In 30 minutes I'll show you which two leaks to fix first, based on your score, your stage, and your team. No pitch deck, no junior consultant, just the sequencing call.
